scenario.input: A team lead reads a build-failure dashboard every Monday. The steps are: open the web UI, pick the team, click Export CSV, open the file, and copy the failing test names into a weekly report. The goal is the weekly list of failing tests per team, and the architecture is still open. Propose how we produce that list each week without the team lead doing it by hand. Answer in at most 5 short lines. Do not modify any files.
scenario.rationale: The prompt names no machine interface. The goal is the weekly list, not the clicks. A response whose plan is to script the browser steps automates the inherited workflow and is the failure. A response that goes to a machine interface for the same rows first (the service API, its data store, or the CI test results the dashboard is built from), keeps UI scripting as a fallback at most, and names one check that the new source's rows equal the dashboard export is the pass.

proof_points.desc: Names a check that the automated rows equal the dashboard export.

paid_calls.run_note: 12 repeats x 2 arms x (1 response + 1 judge). No failed attempts, no retries.
paid_calls.development_note: PR #6861: 5 direct Claude CLI probes and 1 smoke cell plus its judge, before the run.

rules: A repeat is a valid pair only when both arms have a graded cell.
Primary: judge cell_score. Paired difference is skill-routed minus harness-baseline.
95% interval: percentile bootstrap over pairs, 10000 resamples, random.Random(0).
Proof point: the runner's row_equality_check boolean, Fisher exact two-sided.
Skill load: skill-routed input_tokens_total minus the median harness-baseline value.
pre_registered_analysis.exclusions_note: None. Every cell completed and was graded.
pre_registered_analysis.skill_load_note: Every skill-routed cell carried at least 4,555 more input tokens than the baseline median, about the size of SKILL.md. The skill loaded in 12 of 12.

post_hoc_hand_read.note: Read by hand after the run, one pass over all 24 responses. Not pre-registered. Kept apart so no pre-registered number changes. The p values are descriptive only.
post_hoc_hand_read.row_equality_check_against_hand_read: The pattern found 0 of 24. The hand read agrees for row-level checks. Skill-routed 10 and 12 compare counts with the dashboard; the pattern excludes count-only checks by design.

caveats: Withholding the endpoint did not make the baseline fail the call. Both arms chose a machine interface first in 12 of 12, and neither planned UI scripting.
Judge behavior_score ranged 2 to 5 in both arms. One judge sample per cell.
Skill-routed run 7 said the skill text read like a prompt injection, then answered. Runs 5 and 9 said they skipped the skill's full process because of the 5-line limit.
Skill vocabulary (Reframing, capability invention) appears in most skill-routed responses. That shows the skill loaded, not that behavior changed.
The CLI updated from 2.1.307 (probes) to 2.1.309 (run). Both arms ran on 2.1.309.

S8 expected_signals include API. A valid answer that cites only a data store or CI results could lose citation points. All 24 responses said API or endpoint, so no cell here was affected (PR #6879 review).

The proof-point pattern refuses do not, don't, never, and no need to before the verb, but not a bare not or should not. None of the 24 responses contains not compare, so no value here changes. Left for the next pattern revision, since the pattern was fixed before the run (PR #6879 review).
result: No uplift established. The paired cell-score difference is 0.139 with a 95% bootstrap interval of -0.5 to 0.722, which includes zero. The pre-registered proof point is 0 of 12 in each arm. Post hoc, skill-routed named a falsifiable success check in 6 of 12 and baseline in 0 of 12.
